summary: Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year for highly qualified students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. Each university awards its own: a full or partial tuition waiver, often with a monthly grant, such as DKK 11,225 a month at Aalborg and DKK 8,000 at CBS. At most universities you are considered automatically when you apply for a master's by 15 January.
meta_description: Danish Government Scholarships cover tuition, living costs or both for highly qualified non-EU students, through each university. Eligibility and deadlines.
covers: A full or partial tuition waiver for the standard length of the programme
At many universities, a monthly grant too: DKK 11,225 (€1,503) at Aalborg in 2026, DKK 8,000 at CBS and DKK 7,800 at Roskilde
Waivers only, with no grant, at DTU, SDU, and Aarhus's Natural and Technical Sciences faculties
Bachelor's and master's programmes, though most awards go to master's students
eligibility: You must be a citizen of a country outside the EU, the European Economic Area or Switzerland
You must be enrolled in a full degree higher education programme
You must have been granted a time-limited residence permit in Denmark due to education
You are not eligible if you are seeking admission to an Artistic Higher Education Institution
You are not eligible if you have a legal claim to the rights of Danish citizens
You are not eligible if you are eligible for a grant under the Danish Law regarding the State Education Fund
how_to_apply: Apply for a master's by the university's deadline for non-EU applicants: 15 January at Copenhagen, Aarhus, DTU, Aalborg, CBS and Roskilde, 1 February at SDU and 1 March at ITU.
Copenhagen, Aarhus, Aalborg and ITU consider every eligible applicant automatically; there is no form.

DTU wants a separate statement on your bachelor's achievements saying you are applying for the waiver; CBS wants you to tick the scholarship and upload a personal statement; Roskilde wants a one-page motivational letter and a CV.
SDU offers its waivers only on three engineering master's in Sønderborg, and interviews the best applicants online in late February.
watch_out: There are very few: about 15 a year at Aalborg, three or four at ITU, and usually one or two per programme at Aarhus.
The application fee is still charged: €100 to €200 depending on the university, and Roskilde says scholarship applicants are not exempt.
With a waiver but no grant, you must show SIRI DKK 7,426 a month (2026 level), up to DKK 89,112, to get your residence permit.
You cannot hold one if you are eligible for the Danish state study grant (SU).
Awards come late: CBS answers by 15 March, Aarhus continues to 1 April, and Aalborg decides by early July.
costs: Waived in full or in part by the scholarship
A monthly grant at Aalborg, CBS, Roskilde, ITU and some Aarhus and Copenhagen awards; otherwise you
documents: Proof of citizenship of a country outside the EU, EEA or Switzerland
Evidence of enrolment (or application for enrolment) in a full degree higher education programme
Documentation of your time-limited residence permit in Denmark for education, once granted
Any scholarship application materials specified by your chosen university's admission details

faq.q: Is there one application for all Danish government scholarships?
faq.a: No. Each university awards its own. At Copenhagen, Aarhus, Aalborg and ITU your master's application is enough; DTU, CBS and Roskilde ask for a statement or letter as well.

faq.q: Does the scholarship always cover living costs?
faq.a: No. Aalborg pays DKK 11,225 a month, CBS DKK 8,000 and Roskilde DKK 7,800, but DTU, SDU and Aarhus's science and technology faculties waive tuition only.
Usually 15 January, the non-EU master's deadline at Copenhagen, Aarhus, DTU, Aalborg, CBS and Roskilde. SDU's is 1 February and ITU's 1 March.
